To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the anti‐arthritogenic effects of the blood fluke Schistosoma Mansoni in collagen‐induced mouse arthritis are mediated by Th2 cytokines, IL‐4, IL‐13 and IL‐10, but through different pathways, as IL‐17A is reduced by IL‐4/13, and IL‐10 regulates the basal severity of arthritis.
STAT6 and IL‐ 10 are required for Sm infection to suppress CIA via different mechanisms.
STAT6 and IL‐‐10 signaling are required for the suppression, by Schistosoma, of collagen‐induced arthiritis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Th2 cytokines in the regulation of arthritis by a blood fluke.
the role of the Th2 cytokines in the suppression of CIA.
the anti‐inflammatory effects of helminth infection and the underlying mechanisms, and the results may be of use for the development of novel therapies for autoimmune diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

STAT6 is required for the Sm infection‐induced suppression of CIA via the reduction of IL‐ 17A production, whereas IL‐10 is essential for the Sm‐induced anti‐arthritis effects through a yet unknown mechanism.
the helminth‐derived IL‐10 and the helminth itself, via IL‐4, IL‐13 and/or other cytokines, are essential in order for the helminth to suppress arthritis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Sm‐induced suppression of CIA is mediated by IL‐10 and STAT6, but via different mechanisms.
the anti‐arthritogenic effects of the helminth are mediated via a Th2‐dependent mechanism, but that IL‐4/IL‐13 and IL‐10 play distinct roles.
the Sm‐induced reduction in the production of IL‐4/IL‐13 and IL‐10, as well as IL‐17A is essential for the anti‐arthritis effect of Sm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the helminth‐based immunotherapeutic approach to autoimmune diseases may need to take into account the host genetic background.
helminths may be used for the treatment of autoimmune diseases, such as arthritis, but that the mechanisms of their anti‐inflammatory action need to be clarified in detail.
the effects of helminths on the host immune system are complex and depend on the host genetic background.
